chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) addressed the people during the Farewell Pilgrimage, so he said: 'O people! By Allah, there is nothing that brings you closer to Paradise and distances you from the Fire except that I have ordered you with it; and there is nothing that brings you closer to the Fire and distances you from Paradise except that I have forbidden you from it.'

Indeed, the Trustworthy Spirit (Gabriel) breathed into my spirit that no soul shall die until it has completed its sustenance. Therefore, fear Allah and be diligent in seeking (livelihood), and let not the delay of anything from the sustenance cause one of you to seek it through what is not permissible, for what is with Allah is not attained except through obedience to Him.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between sustenance (rizq) and obedience to God in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the completeness of the Prophet's message during the Farewell Pilgrimage, linking the assurance of pre-ordained sustenance (rizq) with the ethical imperative of 'ihsan' (excellence) in seeking it. Shia scholars emphasize that while destiny is fixed, the method of acquisition must be lawful, as true success in attaining divine reward is contingent upon obedience to God rather than mere accumulation of wealth.
